title: Traffic calibration lab notes and hypothesis catalog (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working lab document for calibrating staged traffic exposures, cataloging hypothesis templates, and capturing quick verification checks for cross-functional rollouts (canaries and A/Bs). The goal is a compact, reproducible set of steps and probes teams can reuse when launching LLM-powered features where latency, cost, and quality tradeoffs all matter.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: PMs, product engineers, SREs on-call, ML engineers, data scientists, solutions engineers.
- Scope: small-to-medium staged releases (0.1% -> 50%) for model/route changes, reranker rollout, new safety filters, and routing policy updates. Not intended for full infra upgrades or long-running traffic experiments (>90 days).

Definitions (quick):
- Exposure slice: a traffic cohort defined by routing criteria (country, plan, client-version, intent flag).
- Calibration run: a short ramp with synthetic probes + live-sampled traffic to measure cost/latency/quality.
- Canary pivot: when we switch primary model for traffic slice A -> B after verification.

High-level workflow (one-pager):
1) Hypothesis and metric family defined (PM + ML + Eng).
2) Small calibration run (0.1% - 1%) with synthetic and live probes for 30m.
3) Rapid review: signals check, qualitative review (human raters if needed).
4) Incremental increases (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%) with hold windows and automated checks.
5) Either promote or rollback.

Pre-run checklist (must be green before any ramp):
- [ ] Hypothesis documented (what will change and why).
- [ ] Primary/secondary metrics declared and thresholds set.
- [ ] Fallback route configured (auto-fallback enabled).
- [ ] Observability: dashboard links, synthetic probe runner, alert channels.
- [ ] Stakeholders notified: SRE, PM, ML eng, CS oncall.
- [ ] Cost guardrails set (max spend delta per minute).

Hypothesis templates (compact; fill in per-run):
- H1: "Switching serving model from A->A-quant reduces cost by >=30% without degrading answer relevance (eval_quality_score) by >1 point."
  - Primary metric: eval_quality_score (delta <= -1 allowed)
  - Secondary: token_latency_p50 (< +30ms), fallback_rate (<0.5%)
- H2: "Narrower reranker (top-3) will reduce average inference tokens by 12% and maintain CTR on recommendations (business metric)."
  - Primary metric: recommendation_ctr (delta >= -0.5pp)
  - Secondary: cost_per_1k_tokens, error_rate
- H3: "Safety filter reduces toxic outputs in top-5 responses by 80% with <2% increase in rate-limited responses."
  - Primary: toxic_detection_rate (down >=80%)
  - Secondary: rate_limited_pct (< +2%)

Metric family and quick thresholds (suggested):
- Quality: eval_quality_score (0-100), human-annotator pass rate. Threshold: no drop >1.5 points.
- Latency: token_latency_p50, p95, p99. Thresholds: p50 +30ms OK; p95 must not exceed target SLO by >10%.
- Reliability: error_rate, fallback_rate, timeouts. Thresholds: error_rate < 0.2% for canary.
- Cost: cost_per_1k_tokens, avg_tokens_per_request. Threshold: cost delta relative to baseline budgeted < +20% during test.
- Business signals: conversion, CTR, retention proxies. Must be instrumented for any A/B.

Traffic calibration matrix (example slice plan):
- phase 0 (smoke): synthetic probes only (0%) for 10m
- phase 1 (calibration): 0.1% global sample + targeted slices (dev-only) for 30m
- phase 2 (early canary): 1% (random global) for 1h with hold window
- phase 3 (broad canary): 5% for 4h with automated checks every 15m
- phase 4 (ramp): 20% for 24h with observation windows
- phase 5 (promote): 50% -> full after equivalent confidence

Slice examples (table encoded as text):
- slice: mobile-ios-1.12.x, criteria: client_version <= 1.12.3, reason: controlled diversity, safety profile: medium
- slice: enterprise-paid-APAC, criteria: plan==enterprise && region==APAC, reason: regulated, safety-profile: high
- slice: random-sample-new-users, criteria: is_new_user==true, reason: capture first-time behavior, safety: low

Verification probes (what to run at each phase):
- Synthetic prompts set (10 canonical prompts per feature): measure tokens, latency, deterministic output hash where possible.
- Gold set eval: run pre-labeled prompts to compute eval_quality_score.
- Full trace sampling: capture raw request/response for 0.05% of live traffic (PII redaction enabled).
- Heuristics: length_outlier_pct (>99th), hallucination_detector_flag, fallback_invoke_count.

Quick smoke-checks (paste into runbook chat or ops):
- SQL (example) - baseline vs canary error rate: 
  SELECT slice, COUNT(*) as total, SUM(case when status!='ok' then 1 else 0 end) as errors, ROUND(100.0*SUM(case when status!='ok' then 1 else 0 end)/COUNT(*),3) as error_pct
  FROM inference_requests
  WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 hour' AND experiment='my-canary'
  GROUP BY slice
- Metric diff quick: compute p50 latency diff via metrics API and fail if > threshold.
- Smoke CLI: rinfctl preview-route --route new-model-route --sample 50 --prompts-file smoke.txt

Automated gates (examples):
- Gate A (safety): if toxic_detection_rate increase >0.5% in 30m window -> auto rollback to previous model variant.
- Gate B (latency): if token_latency_p95 exceeds SLO + 10% for two consecutive 15m windows -> pause ramp.
- Gate C (cost): if cost_per_minute > budgeted_spend * 1.6 -> throttle canary traffic to 1% and notify finance.

Human review checklist (short):
- 5 sampled outputs labeled by 2 raters each. Disagreements flagged and discussed.
- 10 edge-case prompts from support queue replayed.
- Any false-positive safety blocks reviewed by policy lead.

Rollback and escalation protocol (compact):
- Owner (oncall + PM) decides rollback if primary metric fails safety gate or business impact is observed.
- Rollback steps: 1) enact route switch to baseline; 2) notify #release-ops with short postmortem stub; 3) open incident ticket if rollback lasted >10m or >5% traffic impacted.
- Post-rollback: capture artifacts (trace samples, golden eval diffs, config diffs) and schedule 48h postmortem.

Communication cadence and runbook links:
- Pre-ramp: update #release-ops channel with run times and links (T-60m).
- During ramp: hourly blips for phases <20%, every 2h for 20%-50%.
- Post-promote: summary + links to dashboards, change log, and who to call if regressions.
- Suggested message template included as a short snippet in the project doc.

Small tooling snippets (pseudocode):
- Synthetic runner:
  for prompt in smoke_prompts:
    for i in range(50):
      resp = call_inference(route=new_route, prompt=prompt)
      record(resp.latency_ms, resp.token_count, safety_flags, resp.hash)
- Auto checker (naive):
  if metric_delta('eval_quality_score') < -1.5 or metric('fallback_rate') > 0.5%:
    trigger_rollback()

Open questions / unresolved:
- What cadence for human rater checks for short-lived canaries (<4h)? (ops prefers 1h; product wants at least 2h)
- Are cost thresholds per-tenant or global for Dedicated customers? Need legal input for enterprise SLAs.
- Should we always run golden eval set in calibration phase for rerankers, or only after 1% canary?

Next steps (action items):
- Aditi to finalize hypothesis template fields in the experiment tracker (CON-1423) by 2025-09-10.
- Jamie to add synthetic probe runner to the CI lab and wire metric exports (2025-09-15).
- Marco to draft a condensed one-page checklist for oncall with explicit rollback commands (2025-09-12).

Notes to self: Keep this doc tight. We want a portable checklist that other feature teams can copy into their experiment protos. Iterate after the next three rollouts.
